# README.md

# How to clone the GitHub Repo

Here are the steps to follow to clone the GitHub Repo onto your local device

1\. On the GitHub landing page, once this repo is open, make sure you can see main at the branch select drop-down. Click on this branch select drop-down and make sure main is selected.  
![][image1]  
2\. Click on the \<\>Code button. Then click on the local tab. Make sure to copy the HTTPS URL.  
![][image2]  
3\. Then head over to the directory you will use to store the repo on your local machine.  
![][image3]  
4\. Once in the folder, right click and select Open Git Bash Here.

5\. Shortly after, you will note a command prompt window open up. 

6\. Once open, type in the following command to clone the repo onto your local machine: git clone \<repository-url\>  
![][image4]

# Setting up the coding environment

We will be using Anaconda Navigator to set up a Jupyter Notebook environment to enable you to run this project. 

Please ensure you have the latest version of Anaconda Navigator installed on your local machine before we proceed. 

1. Open Anaconda Notebook  
2. Once open, navigate to the Environment tab on the left hand side of the page  
   ![][image5]  
3. By default, the base(root) environment will be open. Should you wish to create a specific environment for this project, simply do so by clicking the Create+ button at the bottom of the page. For the purpose of this walk-through, I will be using the base(root) environment.   
   ![][image6]  
4. Using the requirements.txt file, search each of the packages on the list and ensure the version aligns with the version on your Anaconda Navigator. Below is an example of the Pandas library required:   
   ![][image7]  
   The version installed in my Anaconda Navigator is 2.1.4, which correlates to the version I have in the requirements.txt file.   
     
   If this version was not the same, we would simply change the version to align with the version in the requirements.txt file and apply changes.  
5. Repeat for all the libraries listed in the requirements.txt file.  
6. Once the changes have been applied. Return to the Home tab of the Anaconda Navigator Page & launch Jupyter Notebook.  
   ![][image8]  
     
7. Now your environment has been set up and you can run the project Notebook from start to finish.
